source.title: Fully Decoupled Neural Network Learning Using Delayed Gradients
source.authors: Hui-Ping Zhuang; Yi Wang; Qinglai Liu; Shuai Zhang; Zhi-Ping Lin

record.file_problem: Text is the full paper through the appendices; no material truncation apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares a delayed-gradient training recipe against standard back-propagation and reports test errors, including settings where the proposed recipe is better, comparable, or worse. It refines the scope of the generalization comparison but does not test memorization of random labels or the other mapped mechanisms.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's reported classification test-error comparisons for FDG and BP on natural image labels. The cited results from prior work, theoretical convergence analysis, training-error curves, and speed/GPU-utilization measurements are not rows for these claim versions. The paper does not test arbitrary-label memorization.
record.test_reason: The study compares delayed-gradient training with BP, varying gradient shrinking and module count. None of these interventions tests V1–V8. Reporting natural-label test errors, training wide CNNs, and using SGD with fixed batches do not test the specified memorization, width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, dropout, sharpness, or example-removal claims.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: FDG breaks training lockings, gradient shrinking improves reported test performance, and module parallelism accelerates training. Qualify restoration to BP performance: it is incomplete for WRN-28-10 at K=4, and shrinking does not improve MobileNet v2 on Tiny-ImageNet. These are conclusions about FDG, not tests of V1–V8.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares a proposed fully decoupled delayed-gradient training method, with gradient shrinking, against standard BP. It uses SGD on image classification tasks; it does not use the original claim's random-label, width, architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, sharpness, or memorized-example interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Gradient shrinking factor β and number of split modules K change reported test errors; the effect of gradient shrinking is stated to become more significant as K increases.

fits_no_version.finding: With K=2, gradient-shrunk FDG has lower reported test error than rerun BP on the listed CIFAR models. Tiny-ImageNet results are mixed: ResNet-18 reaches 38.22% versus 38.32%, while MobileNet v2 reaches 46.44% versus 46.35%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Suitably chosen gradient shrinking can improve FDG test performance relative to BP in some CNN settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing module count worsens unshrunk FDG test error. Shrinking reduces this loss, but WRN-28-10 at K=4 still has 4.42% error versus BP's 4.01%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient shrinking mitigates accuracy loss from additional delayed-gradient modules, with incomplete recovery in some settings.

fits_no_version.finding: FDG increases ImageNet training throughput over BP; the reported throughput values imply approximately 1.68×, 2.08×, and 2.25× speedups for K=2, 3, and 4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Module-parallel delayed-gradient training can increase throughput on the tested hardware.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
record.problems: No validation set is used; test errors are reported as the median of 3 runs without uncertainty intervals. Several BP table entries use unexplained slash-separated values. The study reports natural-label test errors but does not report training errors in the corresponding tables, so the generalization gap itself is not measured.
record.rows_left_out: Training-speed and GPU-utilization results in Table VII were not cataloged because they do not bear on the listed generalization versions. Training-error learning curves in Figure 3 are not tabulated as separate claim-version outcomes.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe; random-label held-out chance accuracy.
Width variation beyond the zero-training-error threshold and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the role of local connectivity or convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, optimizer switching, and decoupled weight decay.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty; batch size is fixed at 128.
Dropout interventions, small-data effects, underfitting, and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps against other measures.
Removal of highly memorized training examples versus matched random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All row links to none and their claim-relative cannot_determine states are appropriate. The record's tests/T5 classification is not. BP slash entries are explicitly explained as previously reported versus starred rerun results. No listed version has missing evidence requiring an added row or a verdict.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out chance performance.
Width sweep beyond interpolation threshold and test-error behavior.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Sharpness, norm, margin or other measured properties related to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.
